subject: Nanotechnology
title: Supramolecular Chemistry
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Supramolecular Chemistry.

hook.text: Molecules that hold together without covalent bonds — supramolecular chemistry builds with hydrogen bonds and stacking.

buildup.text: Host-guest chemistry uses shape recognition — crown ethers capture ions, cyclodextrins wrap around drug molecules.

discovery.text: Supramolecular polymers assemble and disassemble reversibly — self-healing materials that repair when damaged.

twist.text: Jean-Marie Lehn won the Nobel Prize for this field in 1987 — calling it chemistry beyond the molecule.

climax.text: Supramolecular gels, sensors, and molecular machines all exploit non-covalent assembly for responsive nano materials.

punchline.text: Weak bonds build strong materials — when they work together by the billions.

quiz.question: What makes supramolecular assemblies reversible?
options: They use permanent covalent bonds that can be cut
They rely on weak non-covalent interactions that form and break dynamically
An external enzyme disassembles them on command
